narrative:
The model estimates a 78% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook were your total years of experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and the absence of other job offers. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter careers (half have only 1–5 years), the model sees mid-career professionals like you as more likely to explore new opportunities. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in your present organization also increased the likelihood of departure; this is the most common tenure among those expected to stay, yet the combination with your broader experience signals restlessness to the system.

On the positive side, the fact that you have not received other job offers worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward staying. Most employees the model expects to remain also report no external opportunities.

Taken together, these signals suggest the organization views you as someone who may soon move on. You and your manager should discuss what would increase your sense of commitment and growth here—whether clearer advancement paths, new responsibilities, or changes that address the mid-career plateau the model has noticed. Addressing these points now could shift both your trajectory and future model assessments. (248 words)
